The guide identifies the right court: it quotes the form's own printed caption 'In the Superior Court of Arizona for ______ County' and says to file with the Superior Court clerk in the county the platform wrote there. CONFIRM THE COUNTY-SPECIFIC INTAKE ROUTE BEFORE FILING', and its destination.detail reads 'Local intake varies. Neither the instruction to confirm the county intake route nor the named Maricopa divergence appears anywhere in participant-instructions.md — this lane read the whole 'Where you file this' section. That also interacts with this route's own deliberate blank: the packet leaves the case number for the court to assign, while Maricopa assigns a CIVIL case number through a civil petition form. WHAT WOULD SATISFY IT: carry the registry's confirm-the-county-intake-route instruction and the Maricopa civil-petition detail in the 'Where you file this' section. Guidance only; no PDF byte moves.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: FAILS. vf02's finding STILL STANDS, verbatim, on guidance that has not moved. The committed track registry states rules.fees as 'none. Ask the Superior Court clerk in the county above what the fee is for a petition to expunge marijuana records, and whether a fee-waiver or deferral application applies to you.' That is not a gap, it is contrary money guidance: the record says there is NO fee and NO waiver is needed, and the packet tells the participant there may be a fee and that they may need to apply for a waiver. The guide's own framing compounds it, presenting the answer as unestablished — 'not established in this repository and writing an unsourced figure into a filing instruction would be worse than leaving it out' — when the repository does establish it, by rule number. A participant who reads this may delay filing to arrange money they do not owe, or file a waiver application that does not exist for this route. WHAT WOULD SATISFY IT: state that Rule 36(a)(4) bars a filing fee on this route and that no waiver is needed, and delete the instruction to ask the clerk what the fee is. Guidance only; no PDF byte moves.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.finding: CONVERTED from vf30's FAIL. All three items vf30 named as omitted are now present in participant-instructions.md, under a section that did not exist at d64ea2550. (1) The BCI comparison: 'Compare every Ohio case against the BCI record… and correct the packet if they disagree. The BCI record is not a statutory attachment, but it is the only practical way to assemble the full docket that Ohio Rev. Code Sec. 2953.61 makes decisive.' (2) The charging document: named under 'What you must obtain' as the certified complaint, indictment or information, with the reason — § 2953.321 requires evidence that the offence falls within it, and the substance, quantity and ORC § 2925.11 division are what that evidence must show — and again as a comparison step. (3) The fee: 'Have the fifty dollar filing fee, or your indigency showing, ready for the clerk at filing.' The manifest's remaining requiredBeforeFiling actions are covered too: the signature, transcribing onto the court's own application, attending the 45-to-90-day hearing, and sending the signed order to BCI. Separately, all six field-level REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING blanks in the field map — local caption, arrest date, disposition date, arresting agency, DOB/SSN if the local form requires them, and the § 2953.61 same-act charge schedule — are each disclosed with the printed bracket text that stands in for them on the page.

FILING_DESTINATION.finding: The guide states the registry's rules.filing rather than delegating it: apply to the sentencing court, the application identifies the applicant and the offence, includes evidence that the offence falls within § 2953.321, and requests expungement. It also carries the registry's destination detail honestly — that Ohio has no single mandatory statewide form packet and that the participant must get the current application, caption and filing instructions from that court, which may keep different packets for convictions and non-convictions. The pleading's own caption prints 'IN THE OHIO COURT THAT HANDLED THE CASE — LOCAL CAPTION MUST BE CONFIRMED' rather than guessing a court name, and that blank is declared REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: FAILS, though NOT on the limb vf30 named — that limb is cured. vf30's finding was that the instructions said no held source stated a fee or waiver and delegated both to the clerk while the committed records held the exact answer. The guide now states it: 'Fifty dollars unless indigent. Indigency excuses the fee under Sec. 2953.321(G)', with the statutory allocation of the fee, and it flags that no held source fixes an additional local court fee and names the clerk for that residual question only. That is correct and complete against rules.fees and rules.feeWaiver. WHAT STILL FAILS is the second of this track's two packetInstructions in data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json, which the record itself marks as urgent: '"Sentence" does not include payment of court costs, so unpaid court costs do not delay eligibility. That is a common and expensive misunderstanding and it is worth telling participants explicitly.' This lane searched participant-instructions.md, tracks/oh_marijuana_expungement/participant-instructions.md, companion/companion-guidance.md and the extracted text of the delivered canonical PDF for 'court costs', 'unpaid', 'does not include', 'delay eligibility' and 'misunderstanding': ZERO hits, in all four files, for all five terms. The record holds the answer, names the harm, and directs that participants be told explicitly; the packet is silent. An Ohio participant who owes court costs and is not told this may wait to file, or not file, on a misunderstanding the repository already knows about. WHAT WOULD SATISFY IT: state, in the guide's 'What this costs' section, that 'sentence' does not include payment of court costs and that unpaid court costs therefore do not delay eligibility. Cost: guidance only; no PDF byte moves, and because the pleading fixtures' raster receipt currently binds, keeping the change out of the PDFs preserves that binding.

SERVICE.finding: CONVERTED from vf30's FAIL. The guide now opens the section 'You serve nobody' and states the registry's mechanism rather than delegating it: the court notifies the prosecutor of the hearing, the prosecutor may object by filing an objection with the court before the hearing date, and the hearing is held 45 to 90 days after filing. It also carries the registry's own negative correction — that § 2953.321 sets no sixty-day notice period and no thirty-day objection deadline, and that those figures come from § 2953.32 and do not govern this route — which is the kind of statement a participant reading the neighbouring section would otherwise get wrong. It closes by telling the participant that the drafts generate no certificate of service and that there is no service step to go looking for.

SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: CONVERTED from vf30's FAIL. All NINE of the registry's selfHelpStopConditions are now carried, and this lane compared them term by term against the registry rather than counting: the exact ORC 2925.11 division/substance/quantity, the fifteen-gram hashish line, mixed cases with non-marijuana charges under § 2953.61, dispositions on or after 20 March 2026, one incident producing charges with differing dispositions, pending proceedings or open warrants, prosecutor and victim objection, the sealing-versus-expungement choice, and immigration exposure. They are introduced as carried word for word from the track record, with the file and key named, and the guide adds a true closing line that Ohio expungement has no federal immigration effect and the record may still be reachable in an immigration proceeding. vf30 found a generic 'stop if eligibility is unclear' and none of the nine.
